issues.description: Exposing RevokeErr to API consumers may leak sensitive information
issues.detail: The PR author explicitly raised this concern. Revocation errors can include backend connection strings, credentials, or internal paths from third-party systems (DB, cloud, PKI). Returning RevokeErr verbatim via the API broadens the trust boundary from operator logs to anyone with lease lookup permission. Consider sanitizing or gating behind a capability/sudo check.

issues.description: OpenAPI schema marks 'path' as Required but it can be empty for some leases
issues.detail: The framework path declares `path` with `Required: true`, but FetchLeaseInfo can return an entry where Path is unset (e.g., certain auth/token leases). API schema consumers may treat this as a contract violation. Either drop Required or guarantee Path is always populated.

issues.description: namespace field copied into export but may not be hydrated on disk load path
issues.detail: leaseInfoForExport copies `le.namespace`, but the on-disk Load path (loadEntry) returns a leaseEntry whose unexported `namespace` field is populated via deriveNamespaceFromLeaseID — verify this still happens after the rename. If namespace isn't set on the cold-load branch, `namespace_path` will silently be missing for non-cached leases.

issues.description: Backwards-incompatible rename of exported method FetchLeaseTimes
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method on ExpirationManager. Renaming to FetchLeaseInfo without a deprecation shim breaks any external consumer importing vault as a library (plugins, forks). Consider keeping FetchLeaseTimes as a thin wrapper calling FetchLeaseInfo for one release cycle.

issues.description: Metric name 'expire.fetch-lease-times' no longer matches function name
issues.detail: The metric label is still 'fetch-lease-times' inside FetchLeaseInfo. That's actually correct for dashboard continuity, but worth a code comment so a future cleanup doesn't accidentally rename it and break operator metrics.

issues.description: Test changes mix unrelated context refactor with the rename
issues.detail: In TestExpiration_revokeEntry_rejected_fairsharing the call switches from `namespace.RootContext(nil)` to `namespace.RootContext(t.Context())`. That's a behavioral change (test now has a cancelable context tied to test lifetime) bundled with a pure rename. Either make all test sites consistent or split out.

review.summary: The PR cleanly extends lease lookup with path, namespace_path, and revoke_error and renames FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo. Main concern is the security question the author themselves raised: RevokeErr can plausibly contain sensitive backend details and is now surfaced via API to anyone with lease lookup permission. Secondary concerns are an Required:true schema field that may not always be populated, an exported-method rename with no shim, and a small unrelated context change snuck into the test diff. Test coverage for the new fields is thin — only `path` is asserted.
